hook: The founder of the Persian Empire, remembered by friends and enemies alike as a just king.

pages.t: The baby who should have died
pages.x: The Greek historian Herodotus tells a legend: Cyrus's grandfather, the king of the Medes, dreamed the baby would overthrow him and ordered him killed. The herdsman told to leave him in the mountains raised him instead. Years later, playing at being king with the village boys, the ten-year-old gave himself away by acting too royal.

In real life Cyrus was king of Anshan, a small Persian kingdom under the Medes. Around 550 BC he rose against his overlord, King Astyages. The Median army changed sides and handed Astyages over, and Cyrus took his capital, Ecbatana, and his empire.

pages.t: The richest king in the world
pages.x: Croesus of Lydia, so rich that "rich as Croesus" is still a saying, attacked Persia after an oracle told him he would destroy a great empire. He did: his own. In 546 BC Cyrus took his capital, Sardis, and the gold-mining kingdom with it.

In 539 BC his army entered Babylon, the greatest city on Earth, almost without a fight. Cyrus let the peoples Babylon had deported go home, among them the Jews, who returned to rebuild their Temple in Jerusalem. The Bible calls him "anointed" by God, the only non-Jew given that title.

A clay cylinder written in Babylonian announces how Cyrus restored temples and returned scattered peoples to their homes. It is sometimes called the first charter of human rights, which goes too far, but it shows a conqueror who wanted to be seen as a liberator. A copy is displayed at the United Nations.

Cyrus died in battle in Central Asia around 530 BC. He was buried at his capital, Pasargadae, in a plain stone tomb on six steps. Two hundred years later Alexander the Great found it plundered and ordered it repaired.

Cyrus built the largest empire the world had yet seen, and ruled it by respecting local gods, customs and leaders rather than crushing them. Greeks, Jews and Persians alike remembered him as the model of a good king, and his empire lasted two hundred years.
pts: Freed the Jews exiled in Babylon
A model of tolerant rule for later kings
